## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Vimokkhakathā* ("Discussion of Liberation") is the fifth treatise of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, situated within its first major division (*Mahāvagga*) [SuttaCentral; Collins 1998]. Rather than using the term *vimokkha* ("liberation") solely as an experiential synonym for *nibbāna*, the treatise uses it as an expansive categorical term covering diverse occasions and processes of release [Collins 1998]. These include the successive meditative absorptions (*jhāna*s) and formless attainments culminating in cessation (*nirodhasamāpatti*), as well as the various stages of the supramundane paths and fruits [Collins 1998]. In comparative Buddhist studies, modern scholars have also traced doctrinal connections between the *Vimokkhakathā* and non-Theravāda literature, such as the *Mahāyāna Mahāparinirvāṇa-mahāsūtra* [Radich 2015].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral connect the text to the *Tikapuggalapaññatti* of the *Puggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.3) [SuttaCentral]. Automatically computed analysis by DharmaNexus records 7,785 Pali-internal reuse passages across 208 texts [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, the heaviest reuse occurs with adjacent chapters of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*—particularly the *Gatikathā* (Ps 1.6), *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1), and *Indriyakathā* (Ps 1.4)—as well as canonical sutta formulas found in the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33) and the *Navakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 9) [DharmaNexus]. Post-canonical Pali literature displays substantial verbatim adoption, notably in the *Visuddhimagga* and the commentary *Saddhammappakāsinī* (*Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus include matches with the Sanskrit *Saṅgītisūtra*, the Chinese *Daji famen jing* (T 12), and several Sanskrit and Tibetan versions of the *Prajñāpāramitā* sūtras (including the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*) [DharmaNexus].
